In my wildly inexpert opinion, CNN has a stronger and more insidious bias that Fox and MSNBC combined. Theirs is even more politically motivated. Where MSNBC and FOX are clearly representing variations of loosely defined 'left and right' CNN represents entrenched political entities that straddle the party lines in the USA whose sole goal is making money. This is not in itself a problem as everyone is entitled to try to capitalize on the gifts and freedoms they are given but the problem arises when one considers that there are only three or four really truly massive profit drivers for corporations: private medicine, banking, construction and war profiteering both of which can be lumped together as moving wealth from the average citizen into the hands of Government via taxes levied to pay for the activities of government.

If one examines the paid advertisers on CNN it is obvious that it is these companies which drive the network. Journalism is not dead at CNN or at any other major network and CNN is a valuable source on par with most private news organizations world wide, however I find it will almost always editorially skew toward those stories and opinions which make war and violence seem like the best options. That's just good business. I think that a seasoned observer of news has a responsibility to be aware of the biases of the news organizations which they use. Just in the same way that a citizen has a responsibility to know the biases and opinions of the officials they elect.

This story regarding Russia's destruction of a neutral civilian aircraft serves only to dehumanize the Russian soldiers and command and make the USA/NATO ally Ukraine seem like an even greater victim than it is. This increases the amount of support for a military response to Russian aggression.

I am personally in favour of a halt to Russian expansionism but I see no purpose in military escalation by NATO. Ukraine is not a NATO member. Ukraine made the decision over the last 20 years to be responsible for it's own security and like Georgia in 2008 it was not capable of defending itself against the juggernaut of Russia. In my view there is no justification of risking a confrontation between great powers over these petty border disputes and further more there must be an expectation that collateral damage will occur and is justified in the same way that it is when the same thing happens to Iraqi and Afghani civilians who stray too close active battlefields. MH17 had absolutely no business flying through a warzone and that airline holds almost the exclusive responsibility for the lives they placed in harms way.

TL:DR CNN is biased towards stories that make war with Russia more palatable. Don't be fooled.
